chunks.text: The sun heats water in oceans, rivers and lakes. The warmed water turns into an invisible gas called water vapour and rises into the air.
As water vapour rises it cools down. The cooling vapour condenses into tiny droplets, and billions of these droplets together form clouds.
When the droplets in a cloud join together and grow heavy enough, they fall back to the ground as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
